quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
A circular intersection is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and vehicles with a driver and at least one passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that these parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by driving:

options.text: Through shallow water.
Faster.
Slower.
Through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community service group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or very close to the road ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or very close to the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or very close to the road. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think the children are done getting off.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm extended. Do not move until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: You may park or stop on the freeway shoulder:

options.text: If you turn on your four-way flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You can only park on the freeway shoulder if you have an emergency.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less strong with beer than wine.
Is less strong with wine than beer.
Is strongest with hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol harms your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter — only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you can pass another vehicle from either direction.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean that vehicles traveling in both directions cannot cross the center line to pass.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers:

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: If a vehicle skids on water, the driver should quickly apply the brakes.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, try to regain control. If you cannot, release the accelerator and let the skid stop. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to road conditions ahead. This yellow and black sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid crashes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield for trains.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you see it. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: The most important thing to remember about speed management and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part of the curve.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the posted speed limit before, throughout, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's momentum can make turning difficult, so reducing speed helps you stay in control.

questions.question: A yellow light that flashes on and off means:

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians already in the intersection, and other vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: It is illegal for a person 21 years of age or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. This hand signal means that the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm downward, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you see this signal.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get away from them. Trying to get back at them makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: You can use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when driving at night. Using only parking lights is against the law.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They can use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They can follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles that are using a siren or horn and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when it is safe.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
Drive around a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard if your tire blows out. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down by releasing the accelerator. Then brake gently and move to a safe area.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your signal.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal three to four seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: You are stranded in a snowstorm. What should you do?

options.text: Get out and look for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. It is the safest place to wait for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. It is the safest place to wait for help.
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: When can you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Nothing. Bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as drivers. If they break traffic laws, they can be ticketed just like drivers.

questions.question: Is it against the law to drive at night using only parking lights?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: It is against the law to drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when driving in the dark.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road. It is also illegal to have an open alcohol container in any part of the vehicle.

questions.question: What can you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires properly inflated.
Replace worn tires.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on water instead of gripping the road. Low tire pressure, worn tires, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show other drivers that you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What is a blind spot?

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
The area you see in your rearview mirror.
The area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: A blind spot is an area around your vehicle that you cannot see without moving your head. Blind spots are usually on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop, then proceed when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You can turn in the direction the arrow is pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early so other drivers have time to know you are about to pass.

questions.question: You are waiting at a stop sign in a line of cars. After the cars ahead of you go through and there is no traffic coming, what must you do?

options.text: You can go through without stopping again.
You must stop at the stop sign before going through.
You can slowly roll through the stop sign.
You can follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at the stop sign before going through.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign. Check for traffic before proceeding, even if other cars are moving.

questions.question: When driving through an area with children playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They might run into the street without looking.
They will not cross the street without an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They might run into the street without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand danger and may run into the street suddenly without looking.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one inside.
When it approaches you, even if lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights on a two-lane road. Traffic going both directions must stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.

questions.question: Why should drivers stay extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians happen because drivers did not see them, even when looking. These are smaller than cars and harder to spot. They may also move faster and have less noticeable lights. Drivers must always watch for these smaller, less protected road users.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted to:

options.text: Be loose.
Fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Be hidden under the seat.
Stop the seat belt buzzer or light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: If you are driving too slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull to the right side of the road to let traffic pass.
Not let other cars pass.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road to let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. On a two-lane road with traffic backing up behind you, you must pull off the road to let other vehicles pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When it starts raining while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other cars.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When heavy rain makes it hard to see, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is so heavy that you cannot see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it clears.

questions.question: Which of the following can impair your driving and may lead to a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and liquor
Illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants like glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair driving ability. This includes all alcoholic drinks, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Turn the wheel too far the other way.
Turn the steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to skid, stay calm. Steer the wheel in the direction the skid is moving.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive in the same lane as a motorcycle.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never try to share a lane with a motorcycle, even if there seems to be enough room. Motorcyclists need the full lane width to move safely.

questions.question: When stopped at a railroad crossing with more than one track, you should:

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all the tracks before going.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all the tracks before going.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can clearly see down all tracks before crossing. Even with one track, check again for another train after the first one passes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep hill ahead.
Winding road.
Merging traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill grade is coming up.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield when turning left on green.
One-way.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield when turning left on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to let oncoming traffic pass first. You can complete the turn when it is safe.
